body.target_estimand: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1]\) for any \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\)
body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\omega'\theta(P)=E_P[\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O)]\). On the observable equality model this also equals \(E_P[b(X)'R_P(O)]\) for every integrable feasible loading satisfying \(A'b(X)=\omega\); efficiency is determined separately by projecting the corresponding centered gradient onto \(\mathcal T_P\).

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the OVS target-indexed, period-by-period covariate-conditional one-step DDD parallel-trends restrictions.
sampling_model.units: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed panel units.
sampling_model.treatment: Enabling is absorbing through cohort \(G\), and effective treatment requires \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell entering a retained clean comparison has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For the proved attainment regime, \(X\) has fixed finite support with masses bounded below. Fixed-fold training-cell averages estimate retained propensities, one-step regressions, the augmented period-specific signals \(S_e=g_e+Z_e\), and the conditional moments \(K_P(X)\) and \(r_P(X)\). Thresholding with \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\), estimates the complete-normal coefficient. The shared-cell covariance \(\Gamma_P(X)\) and \(b^\star(X)\) are learned separately for comparator diagnostics; no continuous-covariate attainment claim is made from fourth moments alone.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 establishes identification, Theorem 4.2 establishes asymptotic normality, and Remark 4.6 minimizes variance over constant componentwise clean-comparison weights.

Theorem 3.2 derives the covariate-specific optimal efficient influence function and efficiency bound for staggered DiD, while Theorem 4.1 establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and attainment for the resulting estimator.

Theorem 2 identifies the panel DDD target, Theorem 3 identifies the repeated-cross-section target, Theorem 5 derives the panel efficient influence function, and Theorem 7 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function.
Theorem 5.2 gives variance-minimizing conditional GMM instruments when the conditional covariance is singular and a consistent linear system exists.
Theorem 6.3 derives a fixed-weight stacked-DDD limit law and accounts for dependence from comparison units shared across stacks.
The paper derives an efficient imputation estimator under its event-study model and notes applications to triple-difference designs.
Theorem 3.1 establishes asymptotic linearity and Gaussian approximation for cross-fitted estimators based on orthogonal scores.

body.tldr: The target is a fixed aggregate of staggered-DDD group--time effects under the target-indexed period-specific restrictions of Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna. A finite residual basis \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) exhausts the observed tangent normal, and its Moore--Penrose projection gives the full canonical gradient. Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) remains the optimum inside the smaller aggregate pairwise-score family. In the fixed-finite-support regime, a repaired cross-fitted estimator subtracts \(\widehat\alpha(X)'\widehat S^{\mathrm{per}}\), where the augmented restriction signal has only propensity--regression product drift, and attains the full pointwise bound with a valid Wald interval. The OVS and joint constant loadings have separate aggregate and full equality equations. A bounded binary family yields the exact full-bound gain \(3/512\); positive inference for the estimated efficiency-gap functional remains open because its growing Riesz-map remainder has not been proved.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna establish identification, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise weighting, but do not exhaust the observed tangent space of the overidentified period-specific DDD model or analyze a learned full-normal correction. Existing staggered-DiD efficiency results do not supply the coupled eligibility-gap tangent normal.
project_justification.niche: Eligibility and staggered adoption impose simultaneous conditional restrictions period by period. Cumulative clean-comparison contrasts can span only part of their normal space, so the information bound and an attaining estimator require a complete residual basis and an orthogonal plug-in signal for its estimated centering.
project_justification.fill: The note proves observable tangent exhaustion, derives the singular complete-normal canonical projection, and separates it from conditional generalized least squares within the pairwise-score family. It constructs an explicit orthogonal restriction signal and proves pointwise attainment with cell-average learners for fixed finite covariate support. It also gives exact aggregate and full equality diagnostics and a bounded \(3/512\) witness. Gap-functional Wald inference is not claimed until its full derivative and growing Riesz remainder are controlled.

body.related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise benchmark. The present result differs by exhausting all target-indexed period-specific DDD normals and by learning their correction through an augmented restriction signal. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie give related conditional efficiency results for staggered DiD, but their model does not imply the DDD full-data extension or eligibility-gap tangent calculation. Newey informs generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry; the range inclusion, quotient projection, and learned fixed-support remainder are proved here. Generic DML theory supplies the cross-fitting template but not the all-cohort shared-cell and complete-normal calculations. The bounded binary construction is a full-bound comparison because its sole period-specific normal is exactly the aggregate clean-comparison contrast.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at an interior law and permits singular or redundant complete-normal coordinates. Statistical attainment is proved only for fixed finite covariate support, where cell averages give root-\(n\) conditional-moment rates and a fixed-law positive spectral separation follows from finite support. Uniform inference across rank-changing laws and general continuous-covariate attainment are not claimed. The corrected efficiency-gap construction has valid population tangent coordinates, but its full derivative and estimated growing-dimensional Riesz-map remainder remain unproved, so no positive gap Wald theorem is asserted.
body.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set at interior laws satisfying all observable period-specific conditional DDD equalities and admitting an OVS full-data extension. The canonical gradient and bound are population results. Their cross-fitted attainment and pointwise Wald inference are proved for fixed finite-support covariates with support masses bounded below, cell-average first stages, and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\). The \(b^\star(X)\), OVS, and joint constant loadings are called fully efficient only when the complete-normal equation holds. The \(3/512\) witness satisfies that closure condition. Efficiency-gap pointwise inference and rank-uniform inference remain open.
body.interpretation: There are two precision frontiers. The first minimizes variance among feasible conditional loadings of cumulative pairwise scores and is attained by \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\). The second projects an ambient target gradient against every period-specific restriction normal and yields \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\). A comparator reaches the first frontier when \(N'\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}=0\); it reaches the full bound only when \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\). The fixed-support estimator reaches the second frontier by subtracting a learned multiple of the orthogonal signal \(S_e=g_e+Z_e\), not a raw plug-in residual.
